newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk union, business groups plan protest action.
newsitem.headline: Turk union, business groups plan protest action.

text.p: Leaders of Turkish unions and a business group said on Wednesday they planned joint action to protest at months of political uncertainty surrounding the crumbling Islamist-led coalition, Anatolian news agency said.

It said Fuat Miras, chairman of the Turkish Chambers of Commerce and Bourses Union business group, made the announcement at a meeting with the head of the country's largest union confederation, Turk-Is, and other union groupings.
Mass meetings and work stoppages would be held if political instability continued and other protest measures failed, the agency quoted the groups as saying in a statement.
Turkey's secularist establishment, led by the military, has exerted increasing pressure on the 11-month-old government which has began to buckle under demands for a crackdown on Islamist activism.
Coalition partner Tansu Ciller on Wednesday suggested holding early polls to bring an end to the crisis.
Initially the groups' leaders are to visit President Suleyman Demirel and the speaker of parliament Mustafa Kalemli, Anatolian said.
It said workers and employers would present their views in joint statements at their workplaces next week.
